title: Potato Dynamics Upgrade — Axis/Time Commutators, Interface Contracts and Observable Equivalence
status: archive-generated mathematical contribution extending Potato Dynamics 2.0; established dynamical-systems and contract concepts adapted to the project grammar
abstract: Potato Dynamics distinguishes ordinary time evolution F from Axis/structural flow A, but the earlier framework did not say when those two operations can be applied independently. This upgrade introduces the Lie bracket [F,A] as a quantitative measure of order dependence: when it vanishes, time evolution and Axis transformation commute locally; when it does not, changing scale/description before evolving can differ from evolving before changing scale/description. The upgrade also gives open-system composition an assume-guarantee contract semantics and defines observable equivalence between a full model and a reduced model. Together these additions make three recurring project questions precise: whether structural and temporal evolution are compatible, whether two systems can actually be connected through a Door, and whether a simpler model preserves everything that matters for the declared observable.

axis_time_compatibility.flows: dx/dt=F(x) and dx/ds=A(x) on the same smooth state space when both are defined
axis_time_compatibility.meaning: The bracket measures first-order failure of the two vector fields to commute.
axis_time_compatibility.local_flow_test: Let Phi_F^t and Phi_A^s be the respective flows. The discrepancy Phi_F^t(Phi_A^s(x))-Phi_A^s(Phi_F^t(x)) is of order ts [F,A](x) for small t,s, up to convention/sign and higher-order terms.
axis_time_compatibility.commuting_case: If [F,A]=0 on the relevant domain and regularity conditions hold, the local flows commute: applying Axis then time gives the same result as time then Axis.
axis_time_compatibility.project_interpretation: The Axis is not automatically outside time. The model must test whether structural/scale transformation commutes with temporal dynamics or whether their order changes predictions.

axis_time_examples.pure_rescaling: If A generates a scale transformation and F is exactly scale-equivariant, the bracket may vanish or close on F/A depending on weights. This can justify a clean scale-flow interpretation.
axis_time_examples.noncommuting_case: If temporal dynamics contain a fixed scale or threshold that Axis changes, [F,A] is generally nonzero. Then structural re-description alters the subsequent time evolution and must be modeled explicitly.
axis_time_examples.empirical_test: Estimate both orders on data or simulation and report the commutator defect instead of assuming structural and temporal transformations are interchangeable.

door_interface_contract.contract: C=(A_assume,G_guarantee), where A_assume is the set of admissible interface/environment behaviors and G_guarantee is the behavior the subsystem promises while assumptions hold.
door_interface_contract.system_satisfaction: Subsystem P satisfies C when every allowed trajectory compatible with A_assume also satisfies G_guarantee under the declared semantics.
door_interface_contract.cascade_condition: For a simple cascade P1 -> P2, a sufficient interface compatibility condition is that the output behaviors guaranteed by P1 lie inside the input assumptions required by P2: G1_out subseteq A2_in.
door_interface_contract.unit_type_condition: Interface variables must also match mathematical type, units, timing convention and uncertainty semantics; set inclusion alone does not repair a type mismatch.
door_interface_contract.feedback_warning: Feedback composition requires stronger conditions because each subsystem helps generate the other's environment. Strong/forward-invariant contract semantics are preferable to a one-way compatibility check.

viability_under_composition.warning: Viability of P1 and P2 separately does not imply viability of their interconnection.
viability_under_composition.reason: Coupling can push either subsystem outside the disturbance/input set for which its viability controller was designed.
viability_under_composition.compatibility_margin: Define m_C as the minimum signed distance between realized interface behavior and the boundary of the receiving subsystem's admissible assumption set over the horizon.
viability_under_composition.interpretation: Positive margin means the Door coupling remains inside the declared contract; zero/negative margin marks fragility or contract violation.

observable_equivalence.definition: Models M1 and M2 are (O,epsilon,T)-equivalent over an admissible input class U if matched initial conditions can be chosen so that sup_{u in U} sup_{0<=t<=T} d_Y(O1(x1(t;u)),O2(x2(t;u))) <= epsilon.
observable_equivalence.meaning: Two models need not share internal ontology to be equivalent for a declared observation horizon and tolerance.
observable_equivalence.exact_case: epsilon=0 gives exact observational equivalence for the specified outputs/input class/horizon, not necessarily state-space isomorphism.
observable_equivalence.model_reduction_use: A symbolic/internal component that can be removed while preserving (O,epsilon,T)-equivalence is not empirically necessary for that task.

door_reduction_commutation.criterion: A reduced Door is exact on the tested guard when delta_D=0; it is approximate when sup delta_D<=epsilon_D.
door_reduction_commutation.value: This detects when coarse-graining destroys transition logic even if continuous trajectories look similar away from the Door.

compositional_error_budget.idea: When several approximate modules are composed, assign each interface/model reduction an error tolerance epsilon_i and propagate a declared bound to the final observable rather than treating each approximation as independently harmless.
compositional_error_budget.simple_lipschitz_case: If downstream map H is L-Lipschitz and an upstream reduction introduces error epsilon, downstream output error is at most L epsilon before additional errors are added.
compositional_error_budget.project_value: This creates a quantitative error ledger for multi-room/multi-Door models and prevents hidden approximation debt from accumulating invisibly.

new_research_questions: For a chosen specialization, is [F,A] zero, small or large in the operating regime?
Which Door connections violate assume-guarantee compatibility even though the variables have similar names?
Can a reduced model preserve the target observable through Door events, not just during smooth flow?
What is the smallest subsystem set needed to stay within the final observable error budget?

advancement_gates.axis_gate: Do not claim independent Axis and time flows when their commutator materially changes predictions without modeling that coupling.
advancement_gates.composition_gate: Do not compose subsystems merely because their symbolic roles fit; require interface contract/type compatibility.
advancement_gates.reduction_gate: Prefer the reduced model whenever it meets the declared observable tolerance and the fuller ontology adds no discriminating prediction/control value.
advancement_gates.door_gate: A reduced transition model must preserve reset/guard behavior within tolerance, not only continuous-state averages.

external_references.use: Standard differential-geometric definition of the Lie bracket as the commutator of vector-field actions/flows.
Modern assume-guarantee semantics for hybrid-system interconnections, including distinctions between cascade and feedback composition.
Recent framework connecting assume-guarantee contracts, interconnection effects and resilience margins.

failure_conditions: Axis and time are treated as independent despite a large nonzero commutator in the chosen model.
A composed model violates the receiving subsystem's assumptions or variable units/types.
A complex model is retained even though a reduced model is observationally equivalent within the declared tolerance.
Coarse-graining preserves smooth outputs but fails badly at Door/reset events.
Approximation errors accumulate across composed modules beyond the final error budget.
